identity.description:
Watch the PR and wait for the go-ahead before a fix or a reply (T72)

## Summary

After a run opens its PR, the project lead now watches that PR and its CI on its own. A background monitor polls GitHub every 60 seconds and wakes the session only when something lands: the PR leaving draft, a review, an inline or conversation comment, or a failed check. The project lead verifies each item against the repo, applies a rubric for what is necessary (a bug the PR introduced is fixed; a related small cleanup is taken; an unrelated pre-existing issue and a low-value test are declined with a reason), and then reports its recommendation and waits for your go-ahead before it fixes anything or replies. On the go-ahead it patches the branch, pushes once, and replies to each comment in its own thread, with a marker line that lets the poll skip its own replies. Before this, review findings reached the run only when you pasted them in, and the run acted on them without asking. The whole delivered window moved out of the simple-path reference into its own skill, `crew:delivered-window`, which both paths invoke after the hand-over, and the monitor's 30-minute expiry wake replaces the cron keep-alive as the cache read. A charter line `Gate: off` turns the waiting off for a run you trust.

**Ticket:** [T72 — Watch the PR, and wait for the go-ahead before a fix or a reply](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/blob/main/docs/tickets.md#t72--watch-the-pr-and-wait-for-the-go-ahead-before-a-fix-or-a-reply)
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.104 (this change: the sub-skill, the monitor, the gate, the marker, `Gate: off`, the probe), §15.103 (the keep-alive the monitor replaces), §15.99 (marking the PR ready), §15.92 and §15.94d (the delivered window and patch mode).
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md` owns the delivered window on every path: the watch, the sorting of messages and wakes, patch rounds, the go-ahead gate, the reply on the PR, and the ship word. `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md` owns the exact `gh` and `Monitor` command lines.
- `skills/project-lead/references/skeptical-review.md` owns the necessity rubric and the dispositions ("Adjudication is a ledger"), resume entries 1a and 1b, and the `run.watch.draft` write in "Mark the PR ready".
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md` owns `run.watch`, `rounds[].go_ahead_at`, the `source` and `reply_to` rows, and the charter lines `PR: draft` and `Gate: off`.
- `skills/project-lead/references/autonomy-contract.md` owns escalation trigger 8, `go-ahead (round <round-id>)`.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md` (new): the delivered window, moved whole from `simple-path.md`, plus "Watch the PR", "The go-ahead gate", the held-items rule, and the per-item reply on the PR. Frontmatter `user-invocable: false`.
- `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md` (new): the poll block, the monitor command, the fallback poll, the check-log read, the reply commands, and the marker search for a resumed send.
- `skills/project-lead/references/simple-path.md`: the window section replaced by a six-line pointer; "End the run" invokes the skill.
- `skills/project-lead/references/skeptical-review.md`: the rubric; the gate as a conditional ledger step; resume entries 1a and 1b; "Where a kill lands" rows for them; the `watch.draft` write before `gh pr ready`; pointers.
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md`: the `run.watch` row; `go_ahead_at` on `rounds[]`; `source.ref` and `reply_to` for `pr-comments` and `ci` rounds; the four charter lines; the go-ahead condition in "What a delivered-window round still owes"; Name inventory entries; pointers.
- `skills/project-lead/references/autonomy-contract.md`: trigger 8; pointers.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`: the description names the stop and `Gate: off`; "Take the goal" writes `Gate: off`; pointers. Still 495 lines.
- `skills/project-lead/references/full-path.md`, `skills/project-lead/references/investigation-path.md`: pointers at the skill.
- `CLAUDE.md`: Layout row, Authority entry, Build state sentences for T72 and the probe.
- `README.md`: every sentence that said the run does not stop, that the PR goes ready, or that you paste findings; the `Gate: off` line under "Run one goal in your session"; a "signed-in GitHub CLI" row under "What a run needs"; the Roles row.
- `docs/design.md`: §15.104 (a) to (g).
- `docs/tickets.md`: T72, closed and run; pointers in T54, T60 and T70.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.81 to 0.1.82.

### Constraints that applied

- One rule in one file: the window exists only in the skill; the rubric only in `skeptical-review.md`; the cursor only in the `run.watch` row. A sentence scan found zero sentences shared by `simple-path.md` and the skill.
- `writing-standard.md` "Before you open the PR": container, no duplication, reference depth, size (skill body 497 lines, project-lead `SKILL.md` 495, `CLAUDE.md` 187), ASD-STE100.
- Version bump in both manifests, equal values.
- `crew-record.py` unchanged: `run set watch`, `run set rounds.<id>.go_ahead_at` and `escalation add` already write what the change needs.
- Resume entry numbers unchanged: the new entries are lettered 1a and 1b, so every citation of an entry number still holds.
- Nothing claims more than the probe showed: the fixture has no CI, so a red check is not probed, and §15.104(f) says so.

### How this was verified

- Reading: the project lead read the whole diff against every `Acceptance:` line of the spec (R1 to R11) and the writing checklist, and ran each grep the spec names: no stale pointer at any moved section title; the rubric appears once; the README grep returns only lines that state the new behaviour; the stale-status sweep over the added lines found three "not yet" phrases in kill-table rows, all still true.
- The poll block was run by the IC against crew PR 99 and fixture PR 40: every read parsed, a `ready` line fired from draft state true, a comment line printed once and not on the second poll, and the marker filter dropped a marked comment.
- A live probe, T72's "Run it", by the session that built the change: a project-lead run on `crew-fixture-string-kit` (PR 41, now closed) from `--plugin-dir` at this branch, charter with `PR: draft`. Check 1: `gh pr ready` by hand was reported by the monitor 46 seconds later, and the project lead said the flip was not its own. Check 2: two inline comments reached the project lead in one wake about 70 seconds after posting; its gate report named both, verified the first by running the helper, recommended a fix and a decline, and asked for the go-ahead, with the head unmoved, no reply on the PR, and the record `blocked` on `go-ahead (round pr-comments-r1)`. Check 3: on "Go ahead." the fix landed, one push updated the PR, and each comment got a threaded reply ending in `crew: pr-comments-r1`; the poll reported neither reply. Check 4: `gh pr checks` printed "no checks reported" and exited 1, and the poll printed no `check` line. The monitor's 30-minute expiry re-armed it in a two-call turn (`Monitor`, then "ok"), with one monitor running after. The ship word stopped the monitor and closed the run at $5.18. Record: `~/.claude/crew-t72-probe/add-kebabcase-helper-2bc0`.

### Known gaps

- A failed CI check has not been probed; the fixture has no CI.
- The cron fallback (no `Monitor` tool) has not been run.
- The monitor's task id lives only in the session's context; after a compaction a stray monitor could run until its 30-minute expiry.
- T71 is still open: the scouts, writers and critics this run dispatched stayed idle as teammates.

finding.suggested_fix: Under Gate: off, still gate any round that holds an item from an account other than the principal's own.

finding.claim: Any PR commenter can hide a comment from the watch by ending it with a line starting `crew: `, because the poll skips by marker text rather than by author.
finding.evidence: - An item whose body ends with a line that starts `crew: `. That is your own
finding.suggested_fix: Skip a marked item only when its author is the principal's own gh login, and the round id and item id match a ledger entry.
finding.explanation: The marker can be spoofed, so a third party can keep a review or comment from ever reaching the project lead or the principal.

quotes:
An item whose body ends with a line that starts `crew: `. That is your own
  reply, and "Send the reply file" puts the marker there.
select((.body // "" | gsub("\r"; "") | rtrimstr("\n") | split("\n") | last // "" | startswith("crew: ")) | not)

because you post
    from the principal's own account and the poll skips your replies by the
    marker.
first.rationale: The poll filter (in pr-watch.md and described in SKILL.md) skips any item whose last line starts with `crew: `, with no author check, so any commenter can hide an item from the watch. The impact is limited: the comment stays visible on GitHub, and it only skips the automatic wake, so a careful reviewer would post this as a low-severity hardening suggestion.
